summary: Many of the biggest names in artificial intelligence have signed a short statement warning that their technology could spell the end of the human race. The statement, published by the Center for AI Safety, calls for mitigating the risk of extinction from AI as a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war. It has stoked pushback from experts who argue that focusing on hypothetical worst-case scenarios distracts from more immediate AI risks.

claims.text: A statement signed by almost 400 people, including top AI executives from OpenAI, Google, and Microsoft, warns that AI could lead to human extinction.
claims.evidence_quote: It’s signed by almost 400 people, including some of the biggest names in the field — Sam Altman, CEO of OpenAI, the company behind ChatGPT, as well as top AI executives from Google and Microsoft and 200 academics.

claims.text: The statement says mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside pandemics and nuclear war.
claims.evidence_quote: Mitigating the risk of extinction from AI should be a global priority alongside other societal-scale risks such as pandemics and nuclear war.

claims.text: The statement was posted on the website of the Center for AI Safety, a San Francisco-based nonprofit.
claims.evidence_quote: The statement was posted to the website of the Center for AI Safety, a San Francisco-based nonprofit organization.

claims.text: Meredith Whittaker, president of Signal and chief adviser to the AI Now Institute, mocked the statement as tech leaders overpromising their product.
claims.evidence_quote: Meredith Whittaker, president of the encrypted messaging app Signal and chief adviser to the AI Now Institute, a nonprofit group devoted to ethical AI practices, mocked the statement as tech leaders overpromising their product.

claims.text: Clément Delangue, CEO of Hugging Face, tweeted an edited version of the statement substituting 'AGI' for AI.
claims.evidence_quote: Clément Delangue, co-founder and CEO of the AI company Hugging Face, tweeted a picture of an edited version of the statement subbing in 'AGI' for AI.

claims.text: Two months earlier, a different group including Elon Musk, Steve Wozniak, and Grady Booch signed a petition calling for a pause on large-scale AI research.
claims.evidence_quote: The statement comes two months after a different group of AI and tech leaders, including Tesla owner Elon Musk, Apple co-founder Steve Wozniak, and IBM chief scientist Grady Booch, signed a petition calling for a “pause” on all large-scale AI research that was open to the public.

claims.text: None of the signatories of the earlier pause petition have signed the new statement, and the pause has not happened.
claims.evidence_quote: None of them have yet signed the new statement, and such a pause has not happened.

claims.text: Sam Altman has called for AI regulation and charmed Congress in a Senate hearing.
claims.evidence_quote: Altman, who has repeatedly called for AI to be regulated, charmed Congress earlier this month. He held a private dinner with dozens of House members and was the subject of an amicable Senate hearing, where he became the rare tech executive whom both parties warmed to.

claims.text: Altman said OpenAI could leave the European Union if AI became 'overregulated.'
claims.evidence_quote: Last week, he said that OpenAI could leave the European Union if AI became "overregulated."

claims.text: There is no indication that the United States has imminent plans for large-scale regulation of AI.
claims.evidence_quote: While the White House has announced some plans to address AI, there is no indication that the United States has imminent plans for large-scale regulation of the industry.

claims.text: Gary Marcus, a leading AI critic, said that while potential threats from AI are real, focusing only on a hypothetical worst-case scenario is distracting.
claims.evidence_quote: Gary Marcus, a leading AI critic and a professor emeritus of psychology and neural science at New York University, said that while potential threats from AI are very real, it’s distracting to only worry about a hypothetical worst-case scenario.

claims.text: Microsoft President Brad Smith said deepfakes and disinformation are his biggest worries about AI.
claims.evidence_quote: Microsoft President Brad Smith has said that deepfakes and the potential that they would be used for disinformation are his biggest worries about the technology.

claims.text: Markets briefly dipped after a fake AI-generated image of an explosion near the Pentagon went viral on Twitter.
claims.evidence_quote: Last week, markets briefly dipped after a fake, seemingly AI-generated image of an explosion near the Pentagon went viral on Twitter.
